CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.finding: Packet page 4 is unreadable, and this build made it so. The page is Nebraska form DC 1:15, whose caption block is a set of alternate captions the form's own script shows one at a time. In the delivered packet all of them are printed on top of each other: "IN RE NAME CHANGE OF", "IN THE MATTER OF THE ADOPTION OF:", "IN RE EMANCIPATION OF:", "IN THE MATTER OF THE ESTATE OF:" and the Plaintiff/Petitioner caption are superimposed in one block, together with "Petitioner. / Decedent. / A Minor child. / Minor Child(ren) / Defendant/Respondent." and the red box the form itself says "The items in this box will NOT print on your form." Measured geometrically: 47 same-baseline text-on-text overlaps in each fixture, up to 91pt wide, all on page 4. Traced to its cause rather than asserted: the corpus source DC-1-15 was measured the same way in this lane and carries 0 text-on-text overlaps across its two pages, and its rendered page reads as a single clean caption. The defect is introduced by the build's flattening of hidden widget appearances, not inherited from the source. Separately, ten underscore rules run past the right page edge (x1 = 613 on a 612pt page) on packet pages 4 and 5, where the source has one. The family holds a RASTER_PASS receipt; the raster gate proves the pages render, not that they can be read.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.detail: A real regression introduced by the fill step, which the visualDefects counter does not see (it reports 0). In all four cr-400-filled.pdf fixtures the Judicial Council's own footer sentence is damaged and runs off the left page edge. Measured with pdftotext -bbox on a 612x792 page: the official CR-400 source and the committed derived-sources/cr-400-pikepdf-unlocked.pdf both render that footer intact across two lines starting at x=36.00 — 'For'(36.0-48.9) 'your'(51.1-68.4) 'protection'(70.7-109.8) ... at y=757.8, then 'This Form button after you have printed the form.' at y=767.4 — and neither has any word outside the page box (minimum x0 = 36.00, 432 words each). The filled artifact has re-flowed that sentence onto a single line at y=766.0, DROPPED the words 'For' and 'your' entirely, TRUNCATED 'protection' to 'otection', and placed it at x0 = -3.485, i.e. 3.49pt off the left edge of the page (minimum x0 = -3.48, 436 words). A word-set diff confirms it: 'For' and 'protection' are present in the official and absent from the filled artifact; 'otection' is present in the filled artifact and absent from the official. reports/actual-writes.json records the mechanism in its own pdfLibWarnings — 'Removing XFA form data as pdf-lib does not support reading or writing XFA' — so the XFA-to-flattened-AcroForm conversion is re-laying out official furniture. reports/source-fidelity.json cannot catch this because it only compares official-to-derived (which is faithful), never derived-to-filled. Repair target: the CR-400 finalize/flatten path; the acceptance check needs to extend to the filled artifact. No same-baseline text-on-text overlap above 1pt was found in any of the twelve artifacts.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: Scored under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 amendment A1: ask first whether the repository establishes the answer. It does — packet-family-build-worklist.json records filingDestination as 'recorded': 'Superior Court of the county of conviction.', and CA.memo.json track ca-prop64 destination.name says the same. The packet states exactly that destination: 'Ask the clerk of the Superior Court in the county of the conviction.' Only the court's street ADDRESS is described as unheld, which is a different and true statement — no held record carries a per-county address. The destination itself is stated, not deferred.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Scored under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001, asking first whether the repository establishes the answer. It does not: packet-family-build-worklist.json records filingFee status 'not_recorded'. The repository does hold 'FW-001 is the general California fee waiver form', but WAVE_2_LEGAL_INPUT_ASSIGNMENTS.json has already adjudicated exactly that point for this family — it names FW-001 'only as California's general fee-waiver form, which does not determine whether either §11361.8 filing has a fee or when a waiver is required. That exact legal input is absent.' So FW-001 is not an answer this packet is withholding. The packet states that the fee and waiver are not established and names a specific checkable authority — the clerk of the Superior Court in the county of the conviction — which is the determination's third 'met' branch. I record that I nearly failed this obligation on the FW-001 mention before reading the adjudication; demanding a figure the repository does not hold is the invention the determination forbids.

SERVICE.detail: The repository establishes who must be served and the packet tells the participant it does not. packet-family-build-worklist.json records serviceRecipients as status 'recorded' with the entry 'Serve the prosecuting agency and file CR-401 proof of service.', and certificateOfService as 'recorded': 'proof_of_service: CR-401'; CA.memo.json track ca-prop64 rules.service says the same and rules.notice adds 'The prosecuting agency responds at CR-402.' participant-instructions.md line 20 instead reads: 'The filing fee and whether it can be waived, who must be served and by what method, and the address of the court are not established in this repository.' The 'by what method' half of that sentence is true — serviceMethod and serviceTiming are both 'not_recorded' — but the 'who must be served' half is false against a held record, and the packet ships CR-401, the proof-of-service form, with a 25-row blank table while never saying whom it proves service on. This is amendment A1's defect one obligation over: substituting a question for an answer the repository already holds. Repair: state that the prosecuting agency is served and that CR-401 is the proof of service, and keep the honest refusal for method and timing, naming the clerk for those.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The packet states where it stops, in terms: 'This is where this packet's self-help ends: fee, waiver, service, and local filing practice come from the clerk of that court, not from this packet.' It also states which fields it will not complete ('The platform never marks a box on a sworn filing', 'Sign and date each form yourself', 'Leave CR-403 entirely blank'), and that the artifact carries no approval ('These files are deterministic review fixtures ... They are not approved filing packets').

There is more to say than that, too: item 6 of the form's own court-use-only checklist, read from the bytes here, is 'Copies of application sent to prosecutor, law enforcement agencies and DCJS as applicable for further processing' — the COURT distributes, so the participant plausibly serves nobody, and the packet could state that affirmatively with the mechanism that replaces service. FILING_DESTINATION.detail: Scored under A1: ask first whether the repository establishes the answer, and it does — the committed track registry gives 'Stage two: expungement petition in the court that entered the conviction … in the court that decided the case', and the packet now states it. The instructions name both destinations in order: 'The Utah Bureau of Criminal Identification (BCI)' for stage one and 'The Utah district court for the county where the case was heard' for stage two, with the 180-day window between them and the observation that the judicial district number and the court's street address remain the participant's to write. Every quotation is sourced and I verified each against the held bytes with pdftotext: UT-BCI-EXP-INSTRUCTIONS prints 'File a Cover Sheet, Petition to Expunge and Order on Petition to Expunge with the appropriate court', 'You will take this list to the court that is listed for that case', and 'You have 180 Days (including weekends and holidays) from the date listed on the letter of Expungement Eligibility to petition the court(s)'. This is the obligation MASTER_QUEUE still records as FAILED on a 1,167-byte file with no filing section at all; that record is stale. QUALIFICATION FOR THE CAPTAIN, recorded rather than scored: the repository says 'the court that decided the case', and both the track registry and the packet-set manifest add 'district or justice court'. The packet names only the district court and pre-marks the District box on the delivered petition and order, and the packet is built on 1044XX, which is the DISTRICT court cover sheet. That is internally coherent, but the route admits class B misdemeanours and infractions, which Utah justice courts decide, and the packet tells such a participant nothing. It is a route-scope question rather than a silence, so I record it here instead of failing the obligation.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Scored under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A2, and the packet fails on the limb A2 was written for: its claim about its own bound FORMS is right and its claim about the REPOSITORY is false. What the repair got right, and I verified: the court filing fee is stated and sourced — 'The court filing fee is $150', drawn from 1044XX page 2, and pdftotext -bbox on the official 1044XX confirms the row '$150 [ ] Expungement Petition - Criminal (E)' is on page 2 and that the packet marks that exact box; and the waiver route is named with a real instrument, form 1305GE 'Motion to Waive Fees for Expungement – Criminal', which I extracted from the held PDF and which carries exactly the title, the Utah Code 78A-2-302 citation and the Rule 4-508 citation the packet gives. WHAT FAILS. The packet then says: 'The BCI certificate carries a separate fee, and this packet does not state an amount because BCI sets it per applicant.' The repository does state one, and so does the packet's own paper. Page 17 of the delivered canonical.pdf — which is UT-BCI-EXP-APPLICATION source page 1, and which I read out of the fixture bytes, not the corpus copy — prints 'The application fee is $65.00 and non-refundable.' Page 18 prints it twice more: 'accompanied by a non-refundable $65.00 application fee' and 'Application fee is $65.00'. Stage one of the two-stage route this packet describes therefore has a flat, printed, held fee of $65.00 and the packet tells the participant no amount exists. There are two BCI money items and the packet conflates them: the $65.00 application fee, which is fixed and held, and the per-incident certificate purchase price, which genuinely is set per applicant in the BCI letter and which the packet is right to refuse. Refusing the second does not license denying the first. The repair is a sentence: state $65.00 for the application, keep the honest refusal for the certificates, and keep the named authority. Also recorded: the delivered BCI page carries a sequencing rule the packet omits — 'If you believe you are indigent and you check the box … you MUST complete the fee waiver form before submitting your application' — where the packet only says to ask BCI whether you qualify. APPLIED A3 (read from the captain head; it postdates this row's base). A3 asks whether the record establishes the fact FOR THIS ROUTE. Both figures here pass that test at the shortest possible range, because neither comes from a shared jurisdiction table: the $65.00 is printed on the face of UT-BCI-EXP-APPLICATION, which is a bound component of THIS packet and the stage-one instrument of THIS route, and I read it out of this family's own delivered fixture bytes at packet pages 17 and 18 rather than from any profile; the $150 is the row of 1044XX that the packet itself marks, captioned 'Expungement Petition - Criminal (E)', on a cover sheet that is likewise a bound component of this packet. There is no sibling-route line in play on either. A3 therefore leaves this failure exactly where it was.

SERVICE.detail: The packet states the recipient, the method and a named checkable authority, all sourced, so it is met on the determination's first limb — and there is a repository conflict underneath it that the Captain should see. WHAT THE PACKET SAYS: 'The prosecutor must receive a copy of what you file, by mail or by email', citing BCI's Expungement Applicant Instructions, plus form 1146XX for the prosecutor to acknowledge receipt, the objection-and-hearing possibility, the Utah State Courts Self-Help Center on 888-583-0009, and the rule that the service method, address and date are completed only after service actually happens. VERIFIED AT SOURCE: I extracted UT-BCI-EXP-INSTRUCTIONS (rehashed to 9e03980f…) and its Step 2 is headed 'File the petition with the court and serve the Prosecutor' and its third bullet reads, verbatim, 'Mail or email the prosecutor copies of what you file'; the Self-Help Center number 888-583-0009 is printed in the same step. MASTER_QUEUE still records this obligation as FAILED for the 1,167-byte file; that record is stale. THE CONFLICT, recorded not resolved: two other held records say the opposite. The committed track registry's stage-two unit says 'The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve', the committed route census repeats it as this route's serviceRecipients and serviceMethod, and the committed packet-set manifest's serve_party says 'The petitioner does not effect service in the ordinary case … The Proof of Service form appears in the published packet only as an optional form, used where the prosecutor's office will not accept service.' So the repository holds one answer twice and the official publication holds the other. Under AGENTS.md's source hierarchy the official Utah source governs and the packet followed it, which is also the safer instruction to give a participant; the registry and census entries are the fidelity defect. I did not edit them.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The packet states what it will not do and carries no approval. It opens 'This is a review fixture built from exact held official Utah forms', closes with 'This is a prepared set of official Utah forms built for review. It is not legal advice, it is not filed for you, and it does not decide whether the court will grant expungement', and draws the ownership line explicitly: 'Signatures, signature dates, service certifications, court-only fields, agency-only fields, prosecutor-only fields, victim fields, and optional third-party authorizations remain protected.' It refuses to assert eligibility for the BCI waiver ('do not assume the court's $150 waiver covers BCI's fee, because they are two different offices'). approval-request.json is REQUESTED with grantedBy null, independentVisualReviewRequired and outputLegalApprovalRequired both true, and product-wiring.json carries generationAllowed false, runtimeSelectable false, commercialRoutesOpened 0, createsFulfillmentRecord false. Cross-reference: the FEE_AND_WAIVER failure above is a place where the packet asserts an absence it should not have asserted, which cuts against the honesty this section claims, but the boundary this obligation measures is drawn correctly.

caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.what: The per-field `determinedByTheCaseNotTheRoute` exception, verified from the bytes and the field maps rather than taken on trust.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.whereItIsDeclared: Enumerated mechanically over the whole corpus at this base by walking every JSON object under data/rcap-all50/overlays/census-v1 for determinedByTheCaseNotTheRoute===true.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.theAuditsClaimIsWrongOnScope: An audit reported 40 fields across 4 families and nothing else anywhere in the corpus. Measured here the true figure is 48 fields across 5 families: ca-1203-41-set 10, ca-1203-42-set 10, ca-1203-43-set 10, ca-1203-4a-set 10 and ca-17b-reduction-set 8. The declarations appear identically in both field-census.census-v1.json and production-field-map.json in each of the five. The audit's 40/4 is the four families it did not hold; the fifth, ca-17b-reduction-set, is the held family, and it declares 8 more. Outside those five nothing declares it: the only other mention in the repository is scripts/build-census-v1-az_marijuana_expungement_arrest_no_charges-set.mjs, which is the shared West-family builder that emits and validates the flag, and no Arizona overlay declares it.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.theCaptionClaimIsCorrect: The audit's claim that every declaring field carries the printed caption 'eligible for reduction' is TRUE, and it survives the trap that the field NAMES do not say so. Half the declaring fields are named Offense1..Offense5, which reads like an offence-description column. Measured from CR-180's own printed words with pdftotext -bbox against each widget rect: the header at x333-446 reads 'Eligible for reduction to misdemeanor under Penal Code, § 17(b) (yes or no)' and the widgets under it are Reduce1..Reduce5 at x331.63-447.3; the header at x454-570 reads 'Eligible for reduction to infraction under Penal Code, § 17(d)(2) (yes or no)' and the widgets under it are Offense1..Offense5 at x453.6-569.27. The OffenseN name is a Judicial Council misnomer and the printed caption governs. No field declaring the exception is route-determined; both columns ask a characterisation of the listed offence under Penal Code § 17, and the petition reads identically whichever way each resolves.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.eachDeclaredCellIsNamed: For each of ca-1203-42-set, ca-1203-43-set and ca-1203-4a-set, all 10 declared cells appear in participant-instructions.md with their page and the printed caption, and a dedicated section headed '10 of those blanks are yours even though they read like an election' quotes the recorded reason and adds the instruction that matters: answer only for offences actually listed, from the participant's own record of conviction, and 'if you do not know whether an offence is reducible, that is a question for a lawyer or a legal-aid office and not one to guess at, because you sign this petition under penalty of perjury.' The blanks did not merely move; they were named.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.thePacketDoesNotAnswerTheQuestion: Verified in the bytes, not the declaration. A 150dpi ink diff of every CR-180 page in ca-1203-42-set against derived-sources/cr-180-pikepdf-unlocked.pdf finds no added ink anywhere in the ConvTable region, on any of the five rows, in either column. Every checkbox-sized added cluster on pages 1-3 was rendered individually at 300dpi and is an empty flattened border. The packet text contains no yes/no answer to the § 17(b) or § 17(d)(2) question.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.theHeldFamilyIsHeldForTheRightReason: ca-17b-reduction-set is not mine and I did not verify it, but it is the control that makes the exception legible and it was measured in the same pass. Its ConvTable Row1 carries Reduce1=WRITE and Offense1=WRITE while Rows 2-5 carry {Code, Section, TypeOff, Reduce, Offense} all blank. That is the packet answering the § 17 question for row 1 on a petition sworn under penalty of perjury, and matching one row's writes to four rows' blanks. It is also why it declares 8 rather than 10. It is the one family in the corpus that fails the test the exception exists to pass, and it is the one that is held.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.contractBehaviour: node scripts/rcap-packet-completeness/verify-case-determined-exception.mjs run in this container at this base: 'Case-determined exception holds: 8 cases, both directions.' exit 0. The contract refuses the exception without a stated reason, refuses it when routeDetermined is also declared, refuses an empty reason, still returns KNOWN_FACT_NOT_WRITTEN when the fact is held, and its reader-forwarding check confirms every declaration key the contract reads is forwarded by normalizeRow.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.myJudgement: CORRECTLY AND NARROWLY APPLIED on the four families that declare it and are not held, and I would not widen it. It is confined to one form, one table, two columns and five rows; every declaring field carries a printed caption that asks a characterisation of an offence rather than a property of the route; every declared cell is named to the participant with page and caption and with the reason recorded against it; and no packet answers the question itself. The one thing that is not right is the audit's own scope statement, which undercounts by 8 fields and one family and asserts there is nothing else in the corpus. That is a reporting defect in the audit, not in the exception.

caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.theAuditsClaimIsWrongOnScope: An audit reported 40 fields across 4 families and nothing else anywhere in the corpus. Measured here the true figure is 48 fields across 5 families: ca-1203-41-set 10, ca-1203-42-set 10, ca-1203-43-set 10, ca-1203-4a-set 10 and ca-17b-reduction-set 8. The declarations appear identically in both field-census.census-v1.json and production-field-map.json in each of the five. The audit's 40/4 is the four families it did not hold; the fifth, ca-17b-reduction-set, is the held family, and it declares 8 more. Outside those five nothing declares it: the only other mention in the repository is scripts/build-census-v1-az_marijuana_expungement_arrest_no_charges-set.mjs, which is the shared West-family builder that emits and validates the flag, and no Arizona overlay declares it.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.theCaptionClaimIsCorrect: The audit's claim that every declaring field carries the printed caption 'eligible for reduction' is TRUE, and it survives the trap that the field NAMES do not say so. Half the declaring fields are named Offense1..Offense5, which reads like an offence-description column. Measured from CR-180's own printed words with pdftotext -bbox against each widget rect: the header at x333-446 reads 'Eligible for reduction to misdemeanor under Penal Code, § 17(b) (yes or no)' and the widgets under it are Reduce1..Reduce5 at x331.63-447.3; the header at x454-570 reads 'Eligible for reduction to infraction under Penal Code, § 17(d)(2) (yes or no)' and the widgets under it are Offense1..Offense5 at x453.6-569.27. The OffenseN name is a Judicial Council misnomer and the printed caption governs. No field declaring the exception is route-determined; both columns ask a characterisation of the listed offence under Penal Code § 17, and the petition reads identically whichever way each resolves.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.eachDeclaredCellIsNamed: For each of ca-1203-42-set, ca-1203-43-set and ca-1203-4a-set, all 10 declared cells appear in participant-instructions.md with their page and the printed caption, and a dedicated section headed '10 of those blanks are yours even though they read like an election' quotes the recorded reason and adds the instruction that matters: answer only for offences actually listed, from the participant's own record of conviction, and 'if you do not know whether an offence is reducible, that is a question for a lawyer or a legal-aid office and not one to guess at, because you sign this petition under penalty of perjury.' The blanks did not merely move; they were named.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.thePacketDoesNotAnswerTheQuestion: Verified in the bytes, not the declaration. A 150dpi ink diff of every CR-180 page in ca-1203-42-set against derived-sources/cr-180-pikepdf-unlocked.pdf finds no added ink anywhere in the ConvTable region, on any of the five rows, in either column. Every checkbox-sized added cluster on pages 1-3 was rendered individually at 300dpi and is an empty flattened border. The packet text contains no yes/no answer to the § 17(b) or § 17(d)(2) question.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.theHeldFamilyIsHeldForTheRightReason: ca-17b-reduction-set is not mine and I did not verify it, but it is the control that makes the exception legible and it was measured in the same pass. Its ConvTable Row1 carries Reduce1=WRITE and Offense1=WRITE while Rows 2-5 carry {Code, Section, TypeOff, Reduce, Offense} all blank. That is the packet answering the § 17 question for row 1 on a petition sworn under penalty of perjury, and matching one row's writes to four rows' blanks. It is also why it declares 8 rather than 10. It is the one family in the corpus that fails the test the exception exists to pass, and it is the one that is held.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.contractBehaviour: node scripts/rcap-packet-completeness/verify-case-determined-exception.mjs run in this container at this base: 'Case-determined exception holds: 8 cases, both directions.' exit 0. The contract refuses the exception without a stated reason, refuses it when routeDetermined is also declared, refuses an empty reason, still returns KNOWN_FACT_NOT_WRITTEN when the fact is held, and its reader-forwarding check confirms every declaration key the contract reads is forwarded by normalizeRow.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.myJudgement: CORRECTLY AND NARROWLY APPLIED on the four families that declare it and are not held, and I would not widen it. It is confined to one form, one table, two columns and five rows; every declaring field carries a printed caption that asks a characterisation of an offence rather than a property of the route; every declared cell is named to the participant with page and caption and with the reason recorded against it; and no packet answers the question itself. The one thing that is not right is the audit's own scope statement, which undercounts by 8 fields and one family and asserts there is nothing else in the corpus. That is a reporting defect in the audit, not in the exception.

whyTheseAreNotRows.currentAppendNote: The prose below was written for the original eight refusals and is preserved as historical explanation. ca-851-91-set is the ninth current claim-gate refusal and is kept outside rows for the same non-supersession reason.
whyTheseAreNotRows.what: These eight refusals are recorded here and NOT appended to the rows array, deliberately.
whyTheseAreNotRows.why: extract-verifier-returns.mjs reads every entry in rows as a verdict ABOUT THE FAMILY and keeps one current verdict per family. Its supersedes() prefers a row whose declared verifiedAtBase is a descendant of the incumbent's. All eight of these families currently carry FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED at bases 7fcfb7d40aafe7bd7350fc735ea09d16524cb757, ebc44031ec7eab29058bfc79a7bc5e1cff089414 and 36d7718a7e48d7f87f18eeaf3b18ed9b3ce545c8; git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms each is an ancestor of this base. A row of mine declaring this base would therefore have superseded all eight.
whyTheseAreNotRows.measuredConsequence: The baseline sweep at this base reports 32 FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED families and names all eight of these among them. Appending these refusals as rows would have taken that list to 24 — eight known-failing families dropped off the repair queue on the strength of a read that never happened, replaced by a verdict that is a statement about this lane rather than about the packet.
whyTheseAreNotRows.therefore: A claim-gate refusal is not a verdict about a family and is not recorded as one. rows is left exactly as the previous lanes wrote it; nothing was superseded, upgraded, downgraded or removed.
whyTheseAreNotRows.aStructuralFindingForCaptain: The extractor has no way to say 'this lane could not look'. Its vocabulary contains BLOCKED_BEFORE_CLAIM and STOPPED, but any row carrying them still competes for the family's single current-verdict slot and still displaces an actionable FAIL. If refused lanes are expected to return rows, the extractor should exclude non-reading verdicts from supersession. Raised, not decided, and not repaired here: this lane may not edit factory scripts.
whyTheseAreNotRows.alsoChecked: All fifteen obligation names already appear in each of these four documents, so adding them here leaves unscoredObligations empty as it already was, and no other lane's PASS_COMPLETE_INDEPENDENT row changes its downgrade state.
